title: Addressing Eroom's Law: The Shift Toward Clinically Driven Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery.
authors: He, Jin-Zang; Huo, Zi-Xiang; Wang, Chen-Yu; Ye, Yan-Hong; Shi, Zheng-Jie; Sun, Jia-Lu; Meng, Ze-Yu; Wang, Na-Na; Ming, Han-Yue; Xu, Sen; Meng, Jian-Li; Wang, Shou-Ni
one_liner_zh: 该综述讨论AI驱动药物发现中从靶标结构到临床评估的转变，涉及结构预测和生成模型，但以临床和药物研发流程为主，蛋白质结构计算非核心，方法创新有限。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pharmaceutical Research and Development (R&D) is characterized by high costs, lengthy timelines, and frequent clinical failure. Eroom's Law describes the historical decline in new drug approvals per unit of R&D expenditure. Artificial Intelligence-driven Drug Discovery (AIDD) offers new approaches to target identification, molecular design, and property prediction, but improved computational performance alone does not establish clinical benefit. OBJECTIVE: This narrative review examines how AIDD can facilitate transitioning from target identification to molecular design and clinical evaluation. METHODS: It discusses graph neural networks, structure prediction, and generative models alongside pharmacological and clinical evidence. Four dimensions structure the discussion: target structure and dynamics; subcellular localization and target accessibility; pharmacokinetics and binding kinetics; and clinical factors. They provide a qualitative framework for identifying evidence gaps, not a mathematical model or predictive tool for drug efficacy. A complementary target-molecule-clinical framework illustrates how experimental and clinical evidence can inform earlier stages of drug development. RESULTS: Clinical examples, including rentosertib and GTAEXS617, emphasize distinguishing design objectives, preclinical findings, and clinical observations. Rentosertib's phase IIa trial provides an early clinical signal, although its limited sample size and duration preclude conclusions regarding sustained benefit. Training-data bias, data leakage, limited interpretability, synthetic accessibility, and uncertain generalizability beyond the training domain remain important concerns. This review acknowledges selective coverage of the literature and study-design heterogeneity. CONCLUSION: Assessing whether AIDD can improve overall drug-development efficiency requires comparative evidence on development time, cost, safety, and clinical success. Experimental validation and longitudinal clinical follow-up remain essential for evaluating these outcomes.
abstract_zh: 背景：药物研发（Pharmaceutical Research and Development, R&D）以高成本、长周期和频繁的临床失败为特征。Eroom定律描述了每单位研发支出所批准的新药数量在历史上的下降趋势。人工智能驱动的药物发现（Artificial Intelligence-driven Drug Discovery, AIDD）为目标识别、分子设计和性质预测提供了新方法，但仅凭计算性能的提升并不能确立临床获益。目的：本叙述性综述探讨AIDD如何促进从靶点识别到分子设计及临床评估的过渡。方法：本文讨论了图神经网络、结构预测和生成模型，并结合药理学和临床证据。讨论围绕四个维度展开：靶点结构与动态；亚细胞定位与靶点可及性；药代动力学与结合动力学；以及临床因素。这些维度为识别证据缺口提供了一个定性框架，而非药物疗效的数学模型或预测工具。一个互补的靶点-分子-临床框架展示了实验和临床证据如何为药物开发的早期阶段提供信息。结果：临床案例，包括rentosertib和GTAEXS617，强调了区分设计目标、临床前发现和临床观察的重要性。Rentosertib的IIa期试验提供了早期临床信号，但其有限的样本量和持续时间排除了关于持续获益的结论。训练数据偏差、数据泄漏、可解释性有限、合成可及性以及超出训练领域的不确定泛化性仍是重要关切。本综述承认文献选择存在偏倚及研究设计异质性。结论：评估AIDD是否能提高整体药物开发效率，需要关于开发时间、成本、安全性和临床成功的比较性证据。实验验证和纵向临床随访对于评估这些结果仍然至关重要。
